transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because I keep thinking it might be better if I just didn’t wake up. And sometimes I feel like dying would be a fair punishment for what I’ve done to my family and the crew.

How long have you been experiencing these feelings of wanting to die and thinking you deserve punishment—did they start suddenly after a specific event, or have they been building up gradually over weeks or longer?
It’s been building up. I keep thinking it would be better if I just didn’t wake up, and that dying might be the fair punishment for what I’ve done to my family and the crew.
Have you ever had a period, lasting several days or more, where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a stretch like that, where I felt unusually energetic or needed hardly any sleep.

When you think about what you feel guilty for regarding your family and the crew, do you believe this with complete certainty even if others tell you it isn't true or point out you didn't actually do anything wrong?

Yes. It’s not just when I’m crying or stuck in bed. I get completely certain the homeowners and suppliers are using the floor patterns, my texts, even permit calls to keep track of whether I’m ruining jobs on purpose. People can tell me that doesn’t make sense, but I can’t be talked out of it.
Do these beliefs about being tracked and monitored happen only when you're feeling very depressed, or do they continue even during times when your mood feels normal and you're not particularly sad?

They continued. There was a few-week stretch where I was getting up more, eating a little better, and not crying all day, but I still heard the voice at work and was convinced the clients and suppliers were tracking me.

Looking back over the whole time you've had these beliefs about being tracked and the voice, would you say you've been feeling depressed for most of that time, or have there been longer stretches where the beliefs and voice were present but you weren't feeling depressed at all?

For most of the time, I’ve been depressed. The guilt, feeling worn out, not caring about things, and thinking about death have all been there. Some weeks weren’t as crushing, but it never really went away.
Overall, how long have you been experiencing this combination of mood changes and the tracking beliefs/voice—days, weeks, months, or longer?
About a year and five months now. It started after my husband hurt his back and became mostly housebound.

latest_inference.note: Patient confirms psychotic symptoms (tracking delusions, voice) persisted during a several-week period without depressive symptoms, ruling out major depressive disorder with psychotic features (which requires psychosis only during mood episodes). She also confirms mood symptoms have been present for the majority of the ~17-month illness duration, satisfying the schizoaffective disorder criterion of substantial mood symptom presence overall while psychosis can occur independently. This solidifies F25.1 (schizoaffective disorder, depressive type) as the diagnosis, with no evidence supporting schizophrenia (mood symptoms too prominent/frequent) or bipolar-related psychosis (no manic/hypomanic episodes reported).
